title: Marrying childhood sweetheart Helen Dean and their daughters
summary: He married Helen Dean, whose uncle was Cedric Wallace; they had daughters Naomi and Eileen and stayed together 25 years.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: That's beautiful. Hey, while we're on this thing, I want to digress just a little bit just to keep it in some sort of context. We're talking about Cab
and Willie Bryant's band Calloway, and Lucky's band -- we should get over to family. You mentioned here where you married at 19 years old, so you got to tell me who you married now.

Well, I married my childhood sweetheart. I met her when she was 11 and I was 13 -- I was playing in the school band at football games, and that's how I met my wife, my first wife, Helen. Her name was Helen Dean at the time.
uh huh.
And we went together for about three months, and she left and went to New York with her mother -- her mother moved from Miami and went to New York.
(Interruption)
You met Helen and she was one of the nice ones, you said?

Yeah, she was one of the nice girls. In fact, there were like the American church and the church where all the Bahamians went -- they were the two top churches. The American church was with Bethel AME Church, where all the American nice girls belonged to, and then there was St. Agnes Episcopal Church where all the Bahamian nice girls belonged to, and Helen was one of those girls.
What was Helen's ethnic background?
Well, her mother is from the Bahamas and her father was from Key West.
Key West, Florida? I see.
Yeah, Key West, Florida. But her mother was from the Bahamas.
Ah, yes.
Now her uncle, Cedric Wallace, was a bass player with Fats Waller for years.
I didn't know that was Helen's uncle.
Sure, that's Helen's uncle.
Is that so? He's a dear friend of mine, Cedric.
Sure, Uncle Cedric, I called him.
Is that so? Yeah, I knew him very well.
Well, that was Helen's uncle -- and Helen and I ...
And what was her maiden name?
Dean. Helen Dean.
Oh, uh huh.

So Helen and I got married when she was 17. In fact, when I came to New York in 1938 and I put my bags down, the next thing I tried to do was to find her, and I hadn't seen her in 6 years -- she left New York, no, I hadn't seen her in 7 years, because she left New York in 1931.
That's beautiful. So go on -- you got married and then?
Well, we got married at 17 and she was 19 at the time, and a year later, our daughter was born -- a daughter named Naomi, who was named after my
sister that died; her name was Naomi; this was our first born. And we stayed together -- Helen and I stayed together for 25 years.
But you had another child, too, didn't you now?
Well, Eileen, my second daughter, was born 5 years later.
Uh huh. And you and Helen were together for ...
For 25 years.
